p: 360 Play is all about little ones, so you can plan your visit around their energy rather than anyone else's. Most families find a morning session works brilliantly, letting the kids burn off steam before lunch and leaving the afternoon free for something calmer, or a nap.

Pack socks for everyone, including the grown-ups, because play centres almost always ask for them. A drink bottle for each child and a change of clothes are smart too, especially if water play is part of the plan.

Thinking about age is important. Toddlers and pre-schoolers usually get the most out of the role-play and gentler areas, while older primary children will gravitate towards climbing and the more active zones. If you've got a mix, let each child choose a favourite area so nobody feels left out.

If the weather is good afterwards, Basildon has some great green spaces. Wat Tyler Country Park in Pitsea is a big area of woodland, meadows and marshland beside the creek, with walking trails and plenty of space for a run-around. Gloucester Park, near the town centre, is another good option for a stroll.

Further afield, Langdon Hills offers woodland walks with views over the Thames, and Norsey Wood in nearby Billericay is a lovely ancient woodland for exploring. If the kids still have energy to burn, Southend's seafront is within reach for a seaside finish.
Weekends and school holidays are naturally busier, so if you can visit on a term-time weekday with a pre-schooler, it's often a calmer experience all round.
